title: Ramsey bounds are upward closed in the number of vertices
statement: Fix natural numbers $k$ and $l$, and say that $n$ is a Ramsey bound for $(k,l)$ if every simple graph on $n$ vertices contains either a clique on $k$ vertices or an independent set on $l$ vertices. If $n \le m$ and $n$ is a Ramsey bound for $(k,l)$, then $m$ is also a Ramsey bound for $(k,l)$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a Ramsey bound for (k,l): every graph on n vertices has a k-clique or an l-independent set
replaced:
If $n \le m$ and every graph on $n$ vertices contains a $k$-clique or an
$l$-independent set, then every graph on $m$ vertices does too.
